issues.description: Test fixture `fix.text: '0deg'` is wrong for a `10` -> `10deg` autofix and encodes an incorrect fact.
issues.detail: Two new reject cases (oklch and hsl `from` forms) record `fix.text` as `'0deg'` while the actual replacement should be `'deg'` (or the resulting token `'10deg'`). The range only spans the position after the number. This looks like a copy-paste artifact that either reveals the harness ignores `fix.text`, or will mislead future readers about what the fixer emits.

issues.description: `findHue` conflates the `from <origin>` prefix with the channel triple via an unnamed offset.
issues.detail: `args` mixes the optional relative-color prefix and the channel list, forcing index arithmetic (`0 + offset`, `2 + offset`) keyed off a boolean named `isRelativeColor`. The underlying value is a channel start index. Extracting a small helper that returns `{channels}` (or a named `hueIndex(funcName, args)`) names the actual fact and removes the leaky abstraction.

issues.description: `findHue` has no written contract for which arg position represents hue under relative-color syntax.
issues.detail: The precondition (accepted node shapes) and postcondition (which index is hue) are implicit. The original bug existed precisely because the contract was 'hue is at 0 or 2' rather than 'hue is at 0 or 2 of the channel list'. A short comment stating this invariant, ideally citing the CSS Color 5 grammar, would prevent the same regression for future channel-prefixed syntaxes.

issues.description: Magic offset `2` and weak `'from'` check encode CSS grammar knowledge without documenting it.
issues.detail: `args[0].value.toLowerCase() === 'from'` and the literal `2` assume the first token can only be the relative-color keyword and that origin parsing collapses to one node. Both are true today but uncommented. Name the constant (e.g. `CHANNELS_START_AFTER_FROM`) or guard with an arg-count check and a comment citing the grammar.

issues.description: Missing reject-side coverage for nested relative-color where the outer hue also needs fixing.
issues.detail: Accept covers `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` and reject covers `hsl(from lch(0 0 10) 0 s l)`, but no case exercises both fix sites at once or a relative-color origin nested inside another relative color. One such test would lock the recursive postcondition of `findHue` and prevent regressions when args[0] is a function node.

synthesis.summary: The patch is small, local, and correct for the cases tested: detect `from` as the first arg and shift the hue index by 2. The panel converges on two concerns. First, two test fixtures record `fix.text: '0deg'` where the actual replacement should be `'deg'` — likely a copy-paste artifact that encodes a wrong fact. Second, `findHue` conflates the optional `from <origin>` prefix with the channel triple via an unnamed offset and an undocumented contract; a small helper exposing `{channels}` (or a named `hueIndex`) would name the real value and make future relative-color rules substitutable. No P0s; ships as a point fix, but architecture postpones the same bug for the next channel-prefixed syntax.
